# NIPAT 0.8.2 research distribution evidence

## Review status

**Decision: `accepted-for-research`, scope `pre-1.0-research`.** CI and the joint build identified below completed successfully. The review verified the reports for the four packages and the evidence archive. The JSON acceptance record binds the decision to the actual bytes produced by the build. Desktop tests that were not performed are recorded separately from successful automated checks.

Maintainer Gregorio Dalia requested an official 0.8.2 research release with original sample names in the results, understandable traceability and configurable resources. He authorized a pre-1.0 process that allows extended desktop tests and domain assessment to remain open when their status is explicit and no result is assumed. Codex performed the technical review on that basis. The official channel identifies the distribution decision. Clinical and domain validation remain separate.

## Changes under review

The engine preserves the internal identifiers used by the scientific contracts and linked stages. It also produces readable exports with the original names in filenames, relevant table headers and plot labels. The original inputs retain their filenames. Canonical results remain available and feed downstream stages. Duplicate names receive explicit distinguishing identifiers.

The R presentation adapter operates separately from the vendored scientific scripts. It adjusts labels on copies of the plots, preserves the execution behavior of the original sources and handles long titles. Table exports transform only identifier fields and preserve numerical values. Spreadsheet exports protect names that could be interpreted as formulas. Metadata and HTML reports retain the exact names.

Each run records a sample map and a readable report alongside `run.json` and the logs. Where available, diagnostics capture the container state before removal and verify its identity before cleanup. Exit code 137 is consistent with forced termination. The application identifies an out-of-memory cause as confirmed only when Docker reports `OOMKilled: true`.

Configuration distinguishes physical hardware resources, VM resources and container limits. WSL and Lima changes require a preview, a backup, a check for intervening configuration changes and confirmation. A global WSL restart requires separate confirmation. The application lists affected environments and blocks changes while NIPAT analyses are active. Native Ubuntu applies limits to the analysis without changing Docker's global configuration.

## Automated candidate checks

The following checks passed in the candidate workflows. The table distinguishes simulations, Linux scientific execution and package checks and states what each one establishes.

| Area | Checks performed | Coverage limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client and contracts | Menus, requests, workflows, configuration, results, updates, cancellation and paths on the platforms in the matrix. | Full installer acceptance on every desktop remains outside this test. |
| Resources and diagnostics | Interprocess locking, preview and backup, preservation of unrelated settings, intervening configuration changes, deferred restart, confirmed OOM and unknown termination cause. | Simulated cases do not measure the RAM required for real samples. |
| Scientific computation | Four analyses, composed workflows, synthetic inputs, numerical comparisons and preservation of originals. | The researchers' data require a separate domain assessment. |
| Presentation | Canonical values with and without export, duplicate names, Unicode, long names, text extracted from PDFs and sample associations in downstream stages. | Readability coverage is limited to the tested viewers and sets of names. |
| Windows | PowerShell checks, EXE build and verification of the client with embedded Python. | The checks did not perform a fresh Inno Setup installation and WSL setup on physical Windows 10/11. |
| Ubuntu | DEB installation, use as a non-root user, analyses, reinstallation, removal and upgrade from 0.7.2. | The prepared runner covers its own Ubuntu environment. |
| macOS | Native client tests and ARM64/Intel PKG creation. | Building a PKG does not test Lima startup, Rosetta or the recipient's Gatekeeper policies. |

The Windows report identifies the `staged-embedded-python-client` scenario. All nine payload checks passed, with `wsl_execution: false` and `scientific_execution: false`. The record attributes no new physical Windows test to this candidate.

The Ubuntu reports confirm that all dependency and installation checks passed. The `prepared-ci-runner-real-upgrade` test installed the public 0.7.2 DEB, prepared its runtime, upgraded to 0.8.2 and ran the scientific self-tests. All nine checks passed. Results, preferences, user data and the shared Docker configuration were preserved.

Actual Mac runtime tests for this candidate were **not performed** on either architecture. The acceptance record reports `macos_validation.arm64.status: not-performed` and `macos_validation.x86_64.status: not-performed` with empty evidence lists. Observations from an earlier experimental version apply only to that version.

The `qualification-evidence.zip` archive contains 356 entries of logs, reports and synthetic automated-test data. The descriptor, hashes and Ubuntu upgrade report match the accepted build. The entries' integrity was rechecked locally. The published evidence excludes researchers' private data.

## Historical Windows evidence

The [earlier Windows observation](https://github.com/GregorioDalia/nipat-desktop/blob/1603d998e036ba73d37f015338c1200c1ea12c65/.github/release-acceptance/v0.7.1-evidence.md) identifies commit `1b601081a4aff9efe1806c921fd7ac963feea7b7`, installed by the maintainer on Windows 11 with WSL2. The supplied logs document a ready installation and a successful DNPcall → Contamination workflow on one BAM. The 11 DNP sites and 10 informative sites for Contamination matched the counts from previous separate runs.

That observation provides historical platform evidence. It does not establish installation, resource changes or analysis on the 0.8.2 candidate. The zero estimates in that case do not establish the biological absence of contamination or qualify other samples or workflows.

Comparing the Git bytes at that reference and the candidate identifies **156 changed operational files and 112 unchanged files** in the distribution inventory. Neither `scientific/vendor/` nor the `scientific/SHA256SUMS` manifest changed. The acceptance record lists the full operational differences with before/after hashes. Documentation and `.github` procedures receive separate review. The publisher recomputes the comparison without assuming operational equivalence with the observed version.

## DNPcall and performance measurement

The distributed code separates BAM reading, pileup preparation, R processing and output generation. DNPcall uses `samtools mpileup -l` without `-r`. Its parallel option distributes R processing across samples. It neither splits a single BAM across workers nor parallelizes pileup preparation. This release retains those paths.

Compressed BAM size alone is insufficient to estimate elapsed time or RAM. Readable exports add a second plot rendering, which contributes to total run time. Version 0.8.2 makes no claim of faster DNPcall execution or a measured reduction in memory use.

The optional `scripts/benchmark_workflows.py` tool records DNPcall or DNPcall → Contamination runs on distinct user-supplied BAMs. It captures sample counts, repetitions, options, runtime version, detected resources and stage durations. Total time includes environment preparation and startup. Memory values from R logs are process-reported observations. They do not continuously measure the peak across the whole container.

The benchmark sets no CI performance threshold. The release build does not benchmark private data. This record contains no comparative measurements on real input data and makes no extrapolations to other machines. Local reports include input paths and should be reviewed before sharing.

## Acceptance scope

Package verification resulted in the schema 5 decision `accepted-for-research`. All six complete desktop scenarios in the protocol remain explicitly deferred, including cases with partial automated coverage. Domain assessment remains `pending-domain-researchers`.

Checksums identify the distributed files. They do not constitute a distributor signature. Apple has not notarized the Mac packages. This record does not attest to a GUI, a fully translated interface or complete transactional rollback to a previous version.
